name: Reasoning about space and objects
gist: Teaching models to understand where things are located, how objects relate to each other, and what the physical layout looks like in images.
explain: When you look at an image, you instantly understand the spatial layout. You know that the person is standing in front of the building, or that the cup is to the left of the plate, or that one object is farther away than another. You understand occlusion — when one thing is hidden behind another, you still know both exist. You can predict what is out of frame — if you see the left half of a car, you know roughly where the right half would be. Models need to build this kind of spatial and object reasoning too. This is not just about recognizing what objects are present; it is about understanding their relationships: where they are, how far they are from each other, what they can touch, what is hidden, and what the three-dimensional structure of the scene is.

The challenge is that a camera flattens the three-dimensional world into a two-dimensional image. The model has to learn to invert this projection — to recover the three-dimensional structure from a flat picture. This is inherently ambiguous: a small object close to the camera and a large object far away might look the same size. A model needs to use context, knowledge of typical object sizes, shadows, perspective cues, and other hints to reason about depth. Understanding object relationships is also tricky: a model needs to track multiple objects at once, understand which are in front and which are behind, and reason about interactions. If a person is reaching toward a cup, the model should reason that the person intends to grab the cup. If two objects are far apart, they probably cannot interact. These kinds of spatial and relational conclusions are not explicit in the image; they have to be figured out from context and what the model already knows.

Research in this space builds models with geometric and relational reasoning. Some approaches use scene graphs — a representation that explicitly lists objects and their relationships: 'person standing on floor,' 'cup on table,' 'book to the right of cup.' The model learns to construct these scene graphs from images, and then reasoning about spatial relationships becomes easier. Others use 3D representations internally, learning to estimate depth and reconstruct a three-dimensional model of the scene from the image, even though the input is flat. Some work focuses on visual relationship detection, training models to identify relationships like 'holding,' 'wearing,' 'in front of,' between pairs of objects. Some use knowledge of physics and everyday cause-and-effect to reason about what is likely — a ball on a slope should roll downward. Others combine spatial reasoning with question answering, so that questions like 'how many objects are to the left of the person?' can be answered by reasoning about the layout. The goal is to build models that understand not just what objects are in an image but where they are, how they relate, and what the three-dimensional reality behind the flat picture looks like.

papers.title: Let Language Constrain Geometry: Vision–Language Models as Semantic and Spatial Critics for 3D Generation
papers.contribution: Significantly outperforms existing methods on standard benchmarks while actively steering sampling processes to correct severe spatial errors in both optimization-based and feed-forward 3D generation pipelines.

papers.title: Modality Alignment across Trees on Heterogeneous Hyperbolic Manifolds
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms baselines on taxonomic open-set classification across few-shot and cross-domain settings, with theoretically proven existence and uniqueness of optimal intermediate manifold for alignment.

papers.title: OWL : Geometry-Aware Spatial Reasoning for Audio Large Language Models
papers.contribution: OWL reduces mean direction-of-arrival error by 11 degrees and achieves o'clock-level azimuth estimation while supporting multi-step spatial reasoning.

papers.title: PhaseCoder: Microphone Geometry-Agnostic Spatial Audio Understanding for Multimodal LLMs
papers.contribution: Enables LLMs to perform complex spatial reasoning and targeted transcription from arbitrary microphone arrays, achieving state-of-the-art microphone-invariant localization.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Audio-Geometry-Grid Representation Learning for Universal Sound Source Localization
papers.contribution: Achieves superior performance particularly under unseen conditions, demonstrating the potential of physics-informed representation learning for universal spatial acoustic scene understanding.

papers.title: From Correspondence to Actions: Human-Like Multi-Image Spatial Reasoning in Multi-modal Large Language Models
papers.contribution: HATCH consistently outperforms comparable-sized baselines on three benchmarks and achieves competitive results against larger models while preserving single-image capabilities.

papers.title: GeoSense: Internalizing Geometric Necessity Perception for Multimodal Reasoning
papers.contribution: The method demonstrates significant spatial reasoning gains on multiple benchmarks without compromising 2D visual reasoning capabilities.

papers.title: Mitigating the Modality Gap in Vision–Language Models with Fractal Spectral Geometry
papers.contribution: Theoretically demonstrates alignment of local spectral measures and global fractional Dirichlet energies while preserving multi-scale geometry.

papers.title: On the Generalization Capacities of MLLMs for Spatial Intelligence
papers.contribution: Substantially outperforms naive MLLMs on cross-camera generalization tests, demonstrating that camera-awareness is prerequisite for robust spatial reasoning.

papers.title: Seeing Without Understanding: Disentangling Perception, Reasoning, and Simulation in VLM Gameplay
papers.contribution: Reveals three failure patterns: coordinated spatial drift at 1.5-1.9x chance rate, perception-reasoning dissociation with reasoning capped at 75%, and simulation gap up to 27 points, persisting across model scales and prompting strategies.

papers.title: Thinking with Camera: A Unified Multimodal Model for Camera-Centric Understanding and Generation
papers.contribution: Trained on Puffin-4M (4 million vision-language-camera triplets), outperforms specialized models on camera-centric tasks and generalizes to diverse cross-view tasks.

papers.title: Thinking with Geometry: Active Geometry Integration for Spatial Reasoning
papers.contribution: GeoThinker achieves 72.6 on VSI-Bench with robust generalization across embodied referring and autonomous driving tasks.

papers.title: Unlocking Zero-Shot Geospatial Reasoning via Indirect Rewards
papers.contribution: Achieves extraordinary zero-shot transfer on out-of-distribution benchmarks and surpasses fully supervised specialists on certain benchmarks using only indirect proxy rewards.
